newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Saflife slides on major share issue news.
newsitem.headline: Saflife slides on major share issue news.

text.p: Shares in financial services group, Saflife Ltd, dived almost 20 percent to a five month low on Wednesday on news that the firm is to issue millions of new shares and warrants to raise funds.

Dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said shareholders were concerned that the issue, to raise over 2.4 billion rand to pay for a 30 percent stake in mining house JCI Ltd, would dilute their holdings in the firm.
"The immediate response is that shareholders are not too happy. The amount of money to be raised is big and it will have a fairly substantial dilution effect," one dealer said.

Saflife shares ditched 475 cents or 19.8 percent to a low of 19.25 rand -- its weakest levels since November 12 when it touched 18.70 rand. By 1315 GMT on Wednesday stocks had edged off their lows to 19.75 rand on volume of 176,300 shares.

Saflife said earlier it planned to raise 2.25 billion rand via a rights offer and 154.6 million by way of an offer of warrants to finance black consortium, the African Mining Group's (AMG), purchase of the controlling stake in JCI.
Saflife controls 25.9 percent of Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd, a major member of the AMG grouping, and was earlier earmarked as the vehicle to finance the deal.

Saflife said on Wednesday it would be issuing 112.5 million new shares at 20 rand on the basis of 272.9 shares for every 100 held. A total of 41.2 million warrants will be issued at 3.75 rand on basis of 100 for every 100 shares held. The warrants are convertible into 41.2 million new shares at 20 rand each.
